terms.comment: Also spelled cēpa, with a neuter by-form caepe; the series’ spelling is caepa (Ep. VII). cf. Vulg. Num. 11, 5, where Israel remembers the cucumerēs, pepones, porrī and cēpae of Egypt (cited at Lewis & Short, pepo).
The same word, in the spelling with ē for ae; the neuter caepe (cēpe) is as common.

phrases.latin: Baba in hortō phasēlōs, caepās, cucumerēs colit.
phrases.english: Baba grows beans, onions and cucumbers in the garden (after Ep. VII).

sources: Theodōrus et pater: Epp. VI–VII and Culīna Theodōrī.
Lewis & Short: cepa
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 72; p. 354.
